title: Plant RNA Purification Using TRIzol (TRI Reagent)
author: Diep R R Ganguly
materials: Air-dry pellet at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Nanodrop RNA to check for purity and quantity.

steps.title: Tissue Collection and Grinding
steps.instruction: Collect 50-100 mg of plant tissue and freeze immediately in liquid N2. Grind tissue to a fine powder under liquid N2 using a tissue lyser or mortar and pestle.

steps.title: Initial Lysis
steps.instruction: Immediately add 1 mL TRI reagent (1 mL per 100 mg tissue) to the ground powder.

steps.title: Homogenization and Incubation
steps.instruction: Invert each tube by hand approximately 20x and incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes. Do not vortex samples to avoid RNA degradation.

steps.title: Phase Separation
steps.instruction: Add 1/5 volume of pre-mixed chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (24:1), cap tubes, shake vigorously by hand for 15 seconds until the solution becomes cloudy, and incubate at room temperature for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Centrifugation and Phase Recovery
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 14,000 rcf for 10 minutes at 4°C. Transfer the upper aqueous phase (approx. 400-600 µL) to a new microfuge tube.

substeps.instruction: If buffer and salt carryover is observed (high 230 nm absorbance), reduce the volume of the recovered upper-phase.

steps.title: RNA Precipitation
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of 100% isopropanol and mix by inverting tubes approximately 20x by hand.

steps.title: RNA Pelleting
steps.instruction: Centrifuge samples at 14,000 rcf for 20 minutes at 4°C.

steps.title: RNA Wash
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL of 80% ethanol and invert the tube approximately 10x.

steps.title: Supernatant Removal
steps.instruction: Carefully remove the supernatant, ensuring the pellet does not become dislodged.

steps.title: Pellet Resuspension
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in RNase-free water (e.g., 0.01% DEPC-treated water) or Tris-EDTA (10 mM Tris-Cl, pH 6.5, 0.1 mM EDTA).

steps.title: Optional Concentration Adjustment
steps.instruction: If the expected RNA concentration is ≤10 µg/mL, add 1/10 volume of 3M NaOAc (pH 5.5) and/or 100 µg/mL GlycoBlue (or glycogen).

steps.title: DNase Treatment
steps.instruction: Add 10 μL Buffer RDD and 2.5 μL DNase I stock solution (Qiagen RNase Free DNase Set) and mix with gentle pipetting. Incubate at room temperature for 5-10 minutes.

steps.title: Post-DNase Precipitation
steps.instruction: Add 500 μL of 100% ethanol. Optionally, add 3 μL glycogen or GlycoBlue and 10 μL NaOAc (pH 5.5) to aid precipitation. Mix by gentle inversion.

steps.title: RNA Incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate samples for at least 1 hour at -20 °C (or overnight if purifying small RNAs).

steps.title: Final Pellet Recovery
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 14,000 rcf at 4 °C for 20 minutes. Remove the supernatant and rinse the pellet with 1 mL of 80% ethanol.

steps.title: Final Wash and Drying
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 10,000 rcf for 5 minutes at 4 °C. Remove supernatant without disturbing the pellet and air-dry for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Final Resuspension
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in RNase-free water (e.g., 0.01% DEPC-treated water) or Tris-EDTA (10 mM Tris-Cl, pH 6.5, 0.1 mM EDTA).

steps.title: Sample Preparation for Gel
steps.instruction: Make up the volume of the RNA solution to 87.5 μL with nuclease-free water. Take a 50-100 ng aliquot of RNA and mix 1:1 with 2X RNA loading dye (NEB).

steps.title: Gel Electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Incubate RNA at 65 °C for 5 minutes. Load and run samples on a 1% agarose TBE gel.
